body: Esta aula treina **ouvir e anotar informações (IELTS Listening, TOEFL Listening)**.

blocks.t: Toque em 🔊, ouça e repita cada palavra. Depois tente adivinhar o sentido.

blocks.intro: A conference interpreter talks about her work.
qa: Interviewer: What does simultaneous interpreting demand?
**Split attention.** You listen in one language, speak in another, and **monitor your own output**, all at once. After about thirty minutes **fatigue sets in**, which is why we **work in pairs**.
Our job is to **convey the intent**, not just the words. If a minister is **ironic**, I must be ironic. But I **never add** or **soften** content; that’s **a matter of professional ethics**.
A speaker who **raced through** a text she had **never shared**. I **had to compress** without **distorting**. **Afterwards**, my hands were shaking.

items.q: Interpreters may soften a minister’s content.
Her worst moment involved a fast, unshared text.

blocks.body: Para descrever uma profissão exigente, combine **ações simultâneas**, **princípios éticos** (*never, always*) e **episódios críticos** (*had to + verbo*).
*Interpret* (oral) ≠ *translate* (escrito). Em inglês técnico, a distinção é rigorosa.

body: **Split attention.** — Atenção dividida.
**Keep pace with.** — Acompanhar o ritmo de.
**Lost in translation.** — Perdido na tradução.
**Get the gist.** — Captar a ideia geral.
**Word for word.** — Palavra por palavra.
**Choose one’s words carefully.** — Escolher as palavras com cuidado.
**Walk a tightrope.** — Andar na corda bamba.
**Think on one’s feet.** — Pensar rápido.
**Under the gun.** — Sob pressão intensa.
**Hold the fort.** — Segurar as pontas.
**Can you hear the interpretation clearly?** — Você ouve a interpretação com clareza?
**Will you summarize?** — Você vai resumir?
**Only to compress, never to distort.** — Só para condensar, nunca para distorcer.

blocks.task: Write a 6-sentence profile of a demanding profession (interpreter, air traffic controller, surgeon), including two simultaneous tasks, one ethical principle and one critical episode.
blocks.model: Air traffic controllers track dozens of aircraft while speaking to pilots and coordinating with colleagues. They must never improvise a clearance. After two hours, attention begins to fray, so shifts are short. One controller recalls a night when radar failed; she had to guide planes by voice alone. Afterwards, she said, the silence felt louder than the storm.
